issues.issue: Section 5.1 begins "Notwithstanding any said repossession" and waives damages "upon the occurrence of an event of default under this section," yet Section 5 contains no definition of default and no repossession remedy at all, unlike the enumerated remedy lists in the 2010 Lease and License Agreements. The provision's operative references point to text that is not in the instrument.

The clause indemnifies enforcement costs under "this License Agreement or any related agreements" but cross-defaults only agreements "signed contemporaneously" between the parties; neither "related" nor "contemporaneously" is defined, and the 2010 agreements were signed years earlier. The set of agreements caught by the cross-default is unfixed.

By making a default under "any other agreement signed contemporaneously between Licensor and Licensee" a default here, Section 5.2 presupposes other operative agreements, which cannot be squared with Section 7.7's statement that "[t]his License constitutes the entire agreement between the parties hereto." Whether the earlier ARP Wave agreements remain in force alongside this one turns on reading the two together.

The notice clause supplies an address only "TO LICENSOR" and leaves the Licensee notice block missing entirely, so no address exists at which Licensee may be served under the agreement. The Licensor address given (Apple Valley, MN 55337) also differs from the 55124 zip in the preamble.

The middle of Section 7.1 is unintelligible on the face of the document — the text between "terminated upon" and "any rights herein set forth shall be deemed to be automatically revoked" is garbled beyond reading. What termination events trigger automatic revocation and reassignment cannot be determined from the words.

Section 7.2 requires immediate return of all System(s) "[u]pon termination of this Agreement for any reason," which cannot be squared with Section 1.3, permitting the System(s) to "remain in the possession of the Licensee" at no charge once the original term ends, or with Section 1.1's "non-cancellable" declaration. When the return duty is triggered has to be construed across those provisions.

The clause binds Licensee to "the instructions contained in the ARP Unit Manual" and its "Cautionary and Warning language," a document that is neither defined, attached, nor identified by date or version. The content of the obligation depends wholly on an extrinsic writing.

Section 7.6 permits Licensor to assign "without notice to the Licensee," while Section 7.8 separately governs Licensor assignment as being "without the prior written consent of Licensee," and neither says whether Licensor's obligations survive an assignment. Which of the two overlapping assignment clauses states the operative condition is left to construction.

The integration clause declares this License "the entire agreement between the parties," but Section 5.2 cross-defaults "any related agreements" and "any other agreement signed contemporaneously," and Section 7.9 extends the forum clause to "ANY RELATED AGREEMENTS." Whether the earlier ARP Wave lease and license agreements were superseded cannot be answered from Section 7.7 alone.

Section 7.8's bar on assignment or sublicense by Licensee duplicates Section 1.4, which also declares any attempted transfer "a material breach," while 7.8 attaches no stated consequence, and its Licensor-assignment sentence overlaps Section 7.6. The consequence of a Licensee transfer and the conditions of a Licensor assignment must be pieced together from the several clauses.

The clause compels litigation in Hennepin County of "ALL ACTIONS OR PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT OR ANY RELATED AGREEMENTS," and "related agreements" is nowhere defined or bounded. Whether it captures the separate 2010 individual agreements and the clinic lease and license, and non-contract claims, is open on the text.

The extension of the forum clause to "ANY RELATED AGREEMENTS" presupposes other subsisting agreements, which sits against Section 7.7's declaration that this License is the entire agreement between the parties. Which provision controls determines whether disputes under the earlier agreements are swept into Minnesota.

The blue-pencil sentence directs that a provision "so broad as to be unenforceable" "shall be sufficiently narrowed so as to make it enforceable," without saying who narrows it or by what standard. Applied to the sweeping waivers in Sections 4.2 and 5.1, the degree of narrowing is undetermined.
